plans.design: We perform large-scale quantum simulations of a collapsing shell of matter forming a horizon. We track the entanglement entropy between the infalling quantum field degrees of freedom and the outgoing Hawking radiation. We vary the infall dynamics to control the proper acceleration experienced by quantum modes at the horizon crossing. The simulation incorporates a hypothetical decoherence term tuned to the predicted Quantum Acceleration Threshold (QAT). The procedure: 1) Initialize a CFT (Conformal Field Theory) vacuum state on a lattice in a semi-classical AdS spacetime. 2) Perturb the boundary to model a collapsing shell forming a black hole horizon. 3) Implement a stochastic Schrödinger equation with a decoherence rate Γ = Γ₀ * Θ(a - a_QAT), where a is the proper acceleration of the mode at crossing, Θ is the Heaviside step function, and a_QAT = 10⁴ m/s². 4) Evolve the system and compute the mutual information between the early and late radiation regions. 5) Compare results to control simulations with Γ₀=0 (standard unitary evolution) and to a model with continuous decoherence.

equations.name: Page Curve and Critical Fraction Condition
derivation_steps: In Hawking's original semiclassical calculation, each emitted quantum is entangled with its partner behind the horizon, so the radiation von Neumann entropy grows monotonically: S_Hawking(t) increases with each emitted quantum
For a unitarily evaporating black hole, the total system (BH + radiation) is in a pure state, so S_total = 0
By subadditivity and the Schmidt decomposition, the maximum radiation entropy cannot exceed the remaining BH entropy: S_rad ≤ S_BH(t)
The Page curve follows from the property that for a random state of a bipartite system, S(A) = min(dim A, dim B) – the entropy of the smaller subsystem
The critical fraction condition: the phase transition occurs at the Page time t_Page when S_rad(t_Page) = f · S_BH(0), with f ≈ 1/2 for a symmetric evaporation

Page time: when the dominant saddle in the gravitational path integral switches

equations.name: Island Phase Transition (Replica Wormhole)
derivation_steps: The gravitational path integral is computed using a replica trick with n replicas of the radiation system
Two saddles contribute: (a) no-island saddle giving the Hawking result S_Hawking(t), and (b) an island saddle with an extremal surface ∂I inside the BH
At early times the no-island saddle dominates (S_rad grows); at the Page time the island saddle becomes dominant (S_rad = S_BH, then decreases)
This is a genuine phase transition in the gravitational path integral analogous to a first-order transition

The horizon acts as a quantum error-correcting code that preserves information but distributes it between interior and exterior descriptions.

hypotheses.title: Firewall Paradox (Information Destruction at Horizon)

hypotheses.title: Holographic Boundary Encoding (AdS/CFT Correspondence)
hypotheses.description: Information crossing the horizon is fully encoded on the holographic boundary in a lower-dimensional description. The interior is an emergent phenomenon, and no information is lost—just translated into different degrees of freedom on the boundary.

hypotheses.title: Gravitational Decoherence of Information
hypotheses.description: Information undergoes decoherence due to interaction with the black hole's gravitational field, leading to classicality. Quantum superpositions collapse upon crossing, and information is not fundamentally lost but becomes thermally encoded in Hawking radiation.

hypotheses.title: Quantum Teleportation via Entangled Pair

The claim that information is 'distribut[ed] between interior and exterior descriptions' needs formalization—is this a tensor product factorization failure, or something else? The Page curve behavior requires specific entanglement wedge transitions that aren't derived here.

The scrambling timescale is unspecified. Hayden-Preskill suggests retrieval after O(S log S) time, but the hypothesis doesn't specify whether infalling observers access scrambled information at scrambling time or at a different timescale.

objections: No distinguishing observational signatures are proposed—how would a future experiment differ between this hypothesis and alternatives like ER=EPR or soft-hair mechanisms?
The assertion that infalling observers access information 'only after scrambling' implies a timescale, but no measurable consequence of that timescale is specified.

Hawking radiation spectral measurements (proposed for future black hole analogs) could potentially constrain information encoding, but this hypothesis makes no specific predictions for those experiments.

objections: The AMPS firewall paradox (2012) directly challenges this: if the early Hawking radiation is maximally entangled with late radiation (exterior unitarity), it cannot also be entangled with the infalling vacuum (smooth horizon). Complementarity + quantum error correction must explicitly resolve this tension, and the hypothesis doesn't demonstrate how.

The claim that infalling observers access information 'only after scrambling' seems to conflate two distinct things: (1) when an infalling observer *could* reconstruct the information, and (2) when the information becomes entanglement-accessible in the radiation. These need disambiguation.

The relationship to the recent island formula and quantum extremal surfaces (Penington, Almheiri, Maharlika, Engelhardt, Marolf, Henry) should be addressed—does this hypothesis subsume those developments or operate in tension with them?
required_tests: Explicitly demonstrate how the code structure resolves the monogamy-of-entanglement argument from AMPS—does the infalling observer's reconstruction require access to the early radiation, or not?
Show consistency with the island formula for the Page curve, or explain where it diverges.
Clarify whether this is consistent with AdS/CFT at strong coupling, where the interior is reconstructed from boundary degrees of freedom.

objections: The hypothesis makes no quantitative predictions that could be tested against data, making statistical evaluation impossible at present.

required_tests: Assign prior probabilities to this hypothesis versus alternatives (ER=EPR, remnants, firewalls, soft hair) and specify what experimental outcomes would update those priors.

objections: ER=EPR (Maldacena & Susskind 2013) offers a competing geometric explanation for how information is preserved that doesn't require error-correction language—this hypothesis doesn't demonstrate why its framework is superior or even distinct.

The phrase 'acts as a quantum error-correcting code' may be purely descriptive rather than explanatory—calling the horizon an error-correcting code doesn't explain *why* it is one, any more than saying 'gravity acts like curvature' explains why mass curves spacetime.

The claim that infalling information is 'accessible only after scrambling' potentially undermines the complementarity principle itself—if the infalling observer can access the information, and the exterior observer can access it, then we have a cloning-like scenario unless reconstruction is context-dependent in a way that isn't specified here.
